items.title: pgrecon: open-source Oracle to PostgreSQL migration assessment and schema conversion
items.summary: pgrecon, an Apache-2.0 licensed Oracle to PostgreSQL migration assessment and schema conversion tool, is now public. The current release is 0.7.3.pgrecon works entirely offline. A reviewable, read-only SQL*Plus script produces a dump, and the tool builds a local inventory from it; it never connects to either database. A deterministic rule engine runs 80 rules over the inventory, covering data types and length semantics, storage and partitioning, PL/SQL constructs (parsed with a full grammar, not pattern matching), supplied-package usage, schema objects, and performance posture, each with line-level evidence and remedy guidance. An effort estimator produces person-day ranges from named components with stated assumptions.The converter emits plain PostgreSQL DDL for what it can prove: tables with native partition children, constraints, indexes, sequences, views (CONNECT BY hierarchies become WITH RECURSIVE), materialized views, comments, grants, simple DML triggers, and standalone routines, now including ROWNUM top-N bounds as LIMIT and MERGE statements. Everything it cannot carry faithfully is a named line in a residue report, never emitted DDL.Verification: the full extraction path is verified nightly in CI against Oracle XE 11g, XE 21c, and Oracle Free 23ai; converted output is applied to PostgreSQL 16, 17, and 18 on every commit; a schema fuzzer generates adversarial Oracle estates nightly and checks that nothing crashes, nothing is lost silently, and the DDL applies; and the public benchmark row is measured by a workflow in the repository, which installs Oracle's HR, OE and CO samples plus utPLSQL, PLJSON, Logger and Alexandria into a live Oracle XE 21c, extracts, converts, and applies to PostgreSQL 16: 423 statements, zero rejected, at 0.7.3. Both extraction script tiers capture character versus byte length semantics, so VARCHAR2(30 CHAR) maps to varchar(30).Oracle 9.2 through 23ai are supported through two extraction script tiers; Python 3.11 or newer on the analysis side.Install: pip install pgreconProject page: muzzammil242.github.io/pgreconSource: github.com/Muzzammil242/pgreconRelease notes: pgrecon 0.7.3

items.title: SafeGrd: PostgreSQL backups that are restored and checked on a schedule
items.summary: SafeGrd is a new backup service for PostgreSQL 13 and later that restores every backup ona schedule and checks the row counts.It takes a backup, restores it later into memory or a throwaway database, and counts whatcame back, so you find out a backup is broken before you need it.Taking the backupThe safegrd daemon runs on a host next to your database and connects as a read-onlyrole. On PostgreSQL 14 and later that role only needs pg_read_all_data. On 13 you granteach schema instead. The schema comes from pg_dump and the rows come over binary COPY,in one transaction. After the first run, each backup uploads only what changed.The backup is encrypted with age on your host before itleaves, then written to an S3 bucket with Object Lock on. That can be your own bucket orSafeGrd-hosted storage. The backup data never goes through SafeGrd's servers.You choose how the age key is managed. With a customer-managed key, only you can decryptthese backups. With a SafeGrd-managed key, SafeGrd keeps your key sealed and releases itonly to your enrolled hosts, so you can restore even after losing a host.Supabase, Neon and Amazon RDS work from a connection string. Supabase backups are restoredon Supabase's own Postgres image, so the extensions in the dump load.Testing the backupWe call the restore test a Fire Drill. It takes the newest backup, decrypts it and checksit in one of two ways:In memory. The dump is replayed without a running server, and the table, row and column  counts and the extensions are compared with what the backup recorded.In a sandbox. The backup is restored into a throwaway PostgreSQL database and the counts  are checked there. You can add your own SQL checks too, for example  SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE email IS NULL has to return 0.Each drill writes a signed, dated record with the counts and the check results. Everyrecord points at the one before it. Theattestation verifier checks the wholechain against SafeGrd's published signing key in your browser, with nothing to install.Trying itcurl -fsSL https://safegrd.dev/install.sh | shsafegrd loginsafegrd enrollThe CLI source is on GitHub under the Business SourceLicense 1.1.The free plan covers one database. It is backed up daily to SafeGrd-hosted storage, orhourly to your own bucket, and drilled in memory once a week. Paid plans start at $15 amonth and add hourly backups, sandbox drills and more databases.Docs: safegrd.dev/docs
